newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures rise more late, end stronger.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures rise more late, end stronger.

text.p: IMM currency futures rose further during light afternoon trading to end higher and near day's peaks.

Traders said daily turnover remained light, however, with prices moving on scanty volume estimated on the price boards at about 16,000 June marks, 11,000 Swiss francs, 10,000 yen and less than 5,000 sterling.
One floor broker tied the late move up to some commission house buy orders that triggered buystops in Swiss francs, which popped up again and carried marks higher as well.

The final move up coincided with gain-cutting in U.S. stocks, although brokers tied the currency rise more to position-adjustment before the weekend and into next week's meetings of world bankers and Group of Seven finance ministers in Washington, DC.
"Normally, these G7 weeks are pretty stable weeks," the floor broker added. "The dollar might not make much more headway."
"It (mark) looks pretty firm here," said another floor broker. "Above $0.5900, it would put the dollar rally in question...it could mean consolidation."

Overnight, Japanese finance official Eisuke Sakaibara had said it would be dangerous to assume Japanese rates will stay near record-low levels and that intervention was most effective when markets were not expecting it.
Swiss francs firmed when Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer said it was too soon in the Swiss recovery to tighten monetary policy but that SNB will act when needed.

June yen up $0.000005 at $0.008009, marks up $0.0041 to $0.5865, Swiss added $0.0049 to $0.6913, sterling firmed $0.0014 to $1.6302, Can dollar up $0.0004 at $0.7173, Aussie dollar fell $0.0037 to $0.7723, Mex peso rose $0.000425 to $0.123825.
